title: How do we write four numbers in Roman numerals?
description: Four numbers are written in the Roman system by splitting each into landmark values and giving one symbol to each value, as in the solved example in the book. Nine hundred, ninety and nine use the one-less idea. The video then puts the values back to check each numeral.
teaching_notes: One idea: split the number into landmark values, biggest first, and write one symbol for each. A value just below the next landmark can be written as one less than it, as IV and XL already are. Watch for students who write four symbols in a row for 900 or 90.

video_script.why: The child uses the method of the solved example, taking the biggest landmark that fits again and again, on four new numbers.
video_script.substitution: Split each number into landmark values, biggest first, and write one symbol for each value.
video_script.anchor: four numbers, 1222, 2999, 302 and 715, with the seven Roman symbols and their values in a row
video_script.payoff_line: Take the biggest value that fits, again and again, and write its symbol

final_answer.spoken: part one is em see see ex ex eye eye, part two is em em see em ex see eye ex, part three is see see see eye eye, and part four is dee see see ex vee

never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: (ii) 2999 = 1000 + 1000 + 900 + 90 + 9; 900 is CM (1000 less 100), 90 is XC (100 less 10), 9 is IX (10 less 1), written MMCMXCIX
check: add the values back to get 1222, 2999, 302 and 715
video_script.design: One idea: split into landmark values, biggest first, then one symbol for each. The four numbers stay on the stage and each is split in turn.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four numbers appear: 1222, 2999, 302, 715; a question mark appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about writing numbers in the Roman system.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>The first two are one thousand two hundred twenty two and two thousand nine hundred ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='nums2'/>The last two are three hundred two and seven hundred fifteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we write each one in Roman numerals?

beats.on_screen: the four numbers hold still and the question mark glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board and the question mark glows

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the numbers move to the stage; the symbols are joined to their values: I 1, V 5, X 10, L 50, C 100, D 500, M 1000

marks.small: eye, vee, ex and el are joined to one, five, ten and fifty
marks.big: see, dee and em are joined to one hundred, five hundred and one thousand
marks.way: an arrow shows the biggest value being taken first

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Eye is one, vee is five, ex is ten, and el is fifty.
<bookmark mark='big'/>See is one hundred, dee is five hundred, and em is one thousand.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We take the biggest value that fits, the same way as the example in your book.

marks.given: the facts are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four numbers to write in the Roman system.

beats.on_screen: To find: each number as a Roman numeral

marks.find: the words To find are written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each one in Roman numerals.

marks.m2: a symbol is written under each value: M, C, C, X, X, I, I

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, part one.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>One thousand two hundred twenty two has one thousand, two hundreds, two tens and two ones.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Written with symbols, that is em, see see, ex ex and eye eye.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: (ii) 2999 = 1000 + 1000 + 900 + 90 + 9; 900 is CM, 90 is XC, 9 is IX, so 2999 is MMCMXCIX

marks.m4: 900 is shown as 1000 less 100, and CM is written
marks.m5: 90 is shown as 100 less 10, 9 is shown as 10 less 1, and XC and IX are written
marks.m6: the pieces MM, CM, XC and IX join into one numeral

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, part two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Take two thousands first, and nine hundred, ninety and nine are left.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Nine hundred is one hundred less than one thousand, written see em.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Ninety is ten less than one hundred, written ex see. Nine is one less than ten, written eye ex.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Together that is em em, see em, ex see, eye ex.

marks.m7: 302 is split into 100 + 100 + 100 + 1 + 1, with no tens and no fives
marks.m8: a symbol is written under each value: C, C, C, I, I

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, part three.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>Three hundred two has three hundreds and two ones. No five hundred, ten or five fits.
<bookmark mark='m8'/>Written with symbols, that is see see see eye eye.

marks.m10: a symbol is written under each value: D, C, C, X, V

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, part four.
<bookmark mark='m9'/>Seven hundred fifteen has five hundred, two hundreds, one ten and one five.
<bookmark mark='m10'/>Written with symbols, that is dee, see see, ex and vee.

marks.m11: the values of part one are added back and reach 1222
marks.m12: the values of part two are added back and reach 2999
marks.m13: the values of parts three and four are added back and reach 302 and 715

narration: <bookmark mark='s5'/>Step five, put the values back to check each numeral.
<bookmark mark='m11'/>One thousand plus two hundred plus twenty plus two makes one thousand two hundred twenty two.
<bookmark mark='m12'/>Two thousand plus nine hundred plus ninety plus nine makes two thousand nine hundred ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='m13'/>Three hundred plus two makes three hundred two. Five hundred plus two hundred plus fifteen makes seven hundred fifteen.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Take the biggest value that fits, again and again, and write its symbol.
<bookmark mark='res1'/>Part one is em see see ex ex eye eye. Part two is em em see em ex see eye ex.
<bookmark mark='res2'/>Part three is see see see eye eye. Part four is dee see see ex vee.
